title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
subtitle: Breaded chicken stuffed with ham and Gruyère
excerpt: Chicken breasts pounded flat, rolled around good-quality ham and melting Gruyère, coated in breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried until deeply golden outside with molten cheese inside. A classic for good reason.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken cordon bleu (literally 'blue ribbon chicken') is a Swiss-American dish that became a staple of mid-twentieth century restaurant and hotel cooking across Europe and North America. The dish consists of a pounded chicken breast wrapped around a slice of cooked ham and Swiss cheese (typically Gruyère or Emmental), secured into a roll, coated in breadcrumbs, and pan-fried or baked. The name blue ribbon was applied ironically to mock the pretension of what is, at heart, a simple dish. The technique of pounding the breast flat before rolling is critical; a thick breast will not cook evenly and the cheese will not melt properly. The roll must be tightly sealed at the seam to prevent the cheese from escaping during frying.

content.text: Pound the chicken to an even 5 mm thickness; any thicker and the outside will overcook before the centre is done. Chill the rolled and crumbed bundles for 30 minutes before frying; this helps the crumbs adhere and the roll hold its shape. Use a frying thermometer to keep the oil at a steady 170°C.

items.preparation: 2 large breasts; butterflied and pounded to 5 mm

content.text: Season the pounded chicken on the inside. Lay a slice of ham and then the cheese on each breast. Roll tightly, folding in the sides as you go, to make a neat parcel. Secure the seam with toothpicks.
Coat each roll in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oil to 170°C in a frying pan. Fry the rolls, turning gently, for 6 to 8 minutes until golden all over and cooked through (internal temperature 74°C). Drain on kitchen paper. Remove toothpicks. Serve with a green salad and lemon.
